fatal_errors: The proposed SPD-plus-annealing route does not reconstruct the hexahedron-anvil HPHT treatment.
The specified temperature, pressure, and duration omit the critical 6 GPa, 1473 K, 2 hour processing window.
The proposed reticulated B2 network is materially different from the target hierarchical patterned microstructure with coherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
The HIP comparison changes deformation mode as well as pressure, so it cannot isolate the effect of extreme hydrostatic pressure.
The main supporting evidence for reticulation concerns a compositionally unrelated HfMoTaTiZrCr alloy with a Laves phase rather than the Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni FCC/B2 system.
explanation: The hypothesis correctly recognizes the FCC/B2 lamellar cracking problem, the need to preserve overall composition, and the value of disrupting long crack paths. It is nevertheless a different and weakly supported intervention. The hidden treatment is static HPHT at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours, whereas the proposal relies on severe shear deformation followed by annealing at 800–900 °C and gives no treatment duration. Its mechanism centers on lamellar fragmentation and FCC strain accommodation, missing coherent-interface-mediated dislocation transfer into B2, homogeneous GND evolution, and activation of stacking faults, microbands, and twins. Outcomes are only qualitative and do not recover the approximately 1150 MPa strength, 36% elongation, or distributed-microcracking prediction. The proposed HIP control is also confounded because SPD is removed while pressure and deformation history change; an informative test would compare 6 GPa HPHT against lower-pressure conventional HIP at matched temperature, time, and thermal history, followed by interface-coherency, GND-density, tensile, and fracture-surface measurements. The cross-alloy Laves-phase analogy establishes novelty but does not validate B2 reticulation in this alloy.
